description: This full-day event will introduce a vision for genome surgery at UCSF. UCSF Center for Genome Surgery is a new partnership between the UCSF Broad Stem Cell Center and the Innovative Genomics Institute, dedicated to building a pathway to bring genetically-targeted therapies to people with genetic diseases. Symposium Highlights Welcome by Chancellor Sam Hawgood Opening session: Why a Center for Genome Surgery? Keynote Addresses from Jennifer Doudna and Laura Sepp-Lorenzino Scientific talks and discussions on genome engineering technologies, research priorities, and building systems for clinical implementation Discussions of ethics, patient perspectives, and the future of individualized genome editing Closing conversation on building the long-term vision for the Center Poster session Closing reception Poster Presentations: Faculty, trainees, and research staff are invited to submit abstracts for consideration in the poster session by August 14. Presentations ranging from basic science discovery research through clinical implementation in genetic medicine are welcome. Topics may include disease biology, therapeutic engineering, genome editing, gene replacement, RNA therapeutics, cell therapies, delivery technologies, manufacturing, regulatory science, ethics, and multidisciplinary approaches to clinical translation. We particularly encourage work that bridges scientific discovery with the development therapies for patients with genetic disease. The symposium is designed to bring together investigators from academia, healthcare, industry, regulatory, and patient advocacy organizations to foster discussion and collaboration around the development and translation of genetic medicines. Authors should therefore submit abstracts and data that are appropriate for presentation to this broad audience. Submit abstract. Lunch will be provided for those who register. If you need a reasonable accommodation to participate in this event because of a disability, please contact GenomeSurgery@ucsf.edu as soon as possible.
